hook-0.text: KashLink sends USDC as a link. No address, no account, no gas. Live on Arc mainnet.

problem-0.text: Every cash-link product has the same problem.

problem-1.text: The link is a fresh address. It holds the money, but has no gas to move it.

problem-2.text: So you bolt on a relayer, a hot wallet, meta-transactions, and an API. Our Polygon version needed all four.

problem-3.text: Arc makes every one of them unnecessary.

arc-0.text: On Arc, USDC is the gas.

arc-1.text: The sender funds the link once: the amount, a one percent fee, and one cent per slot.

arc-2.text: The contract drops that cent on the link's own address. And that cent is the gas for the claim.

arc-3.text: The recipient signs one plain transaction with the key in the link. The chain just accepts it.

arc-4.text: No relayer. No second token. No wallet to install first.

demo-0.text: Fund it once. Pick USDC or E-U-R-C, an amount, and who: one person, a link each, or an open drop.

demo-1.text: One transaction funds everything: the money, the fee, and a cent of claim gas per person.

demo-2.text: The key rides in the URL and never touches a server. Share it by chat, or hold up the QR code.

claim-0.text: For the recipient, the link arrives like any message. Nothing to install.

claim-1.text: No wallet? Face ID creates a passkey wallet on the spot, and the claim goes straight into it.

claim-2.text: One plain transaction, paid from the cent on the link. Instant finality: received a block later.

features-0.text: Cash links. A link each. Open drops. Notes and QR codes. Returns. Passkey wallets. E-U-R-C. And live stats.

contract-0.text: About 260 lines of Solidity, 39 Foundry tests, no proxy, no pause. The app never holds the money.

contract-1.text: The only ways out of escrow are a claim with the link key, or a refund to the sender after expiry.

contract-2.text: It's live on Arc mainnet, and keeps its own totals, so the stats page needs no backend.

outro-0.text: KashLink. Send USDC as a link. Share it like cash.
